newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 21.

text.p: Wall Street is awaiting a presentation to be made on Monday by IBM Corp's chief financial officer, Richard Thoman, about the company's performance, the Wall Street Journal reported Monday.
Other top stories included:
- PepsiCo Inc agreed to put $40 million into its Latin American bottler, Buenos Aires Embotelladora SA (Baesa).
- Neurocrine Biosciences Inc is expected to receive up to $74 million to develop new drugs for obesity and Alzheimer's disease.
- General Motors Corp is revamping the way it gets vehicles to dealers so as to deliver the precise car that a client has ordered in 24 hours.
- Big Tobacco might have to forget its argument that smoking is simply a "risk factor" for disease in light of the latest scientific findings showing a genetic link between smoking and cancer.
- Cisco Systems Inc and Gillette Co are among a growing number of companies that have suspended share buybacks.
- Companies in several industries might have invested too much in new plants and equipment.
- Money fund assets have grown in recent months and could reach the $1 trillion mark by next year.
- Salomon Phibro Oil Trust dismissed 20 percent of its employees, while Lehman disbanded its precious metals group in the latest cutbacks in the commodity business.
- Spain's Endes made a $1.5 billion takevover bid for two regional electrical utilities.
- Canada's Agrium Inc agreed to buy Viridian Inc for $887.4 million in stock.
- Hershey Foods Corp agreed to buy the North American operations of Huhtamaki in a deal worth $330 million.
- Solv-Ex Corp's stock fell last week after Deutsche Morgan Grenfell bought 12.4 percent of it.
- Xerox Corp reported a 2.3-percent drop in quarterly profit for its core business.
- McDonald's Corp reported a poor quarter as international sales were soft. - New York Times Co said its profit increased 37 percent, excluding special items.
- A U.S. federal judge rejected a plea of no contest from Ajinomoto Co Inc accused of colluding with Archer Daniels Midland Co to rig the lysine market.
- The U.S. Energy Department will study Nymex oil futures trading to find out if it discourages refiners from buildling heating oil stocks.
- A U.S. federal appeals court rejected a $115 million fine against DuPont Co over its Benlate fungicide.
- Internet access more than doubled to 14.7 million U.S. households in the past rea.
- General Motors Corp and the Canadian Automobile Workers union held intense talk over the weekend to reach a new labor contract.
- The U.S. trade deficit narrowed in August.
- The Dow Jones industrial average closed 35.03 points higher to a record 6,094.32 on late buying on Friday.
- Fund managers of emerging market debt do not expect to get such high returns on their investments as they have during the past 12 months.
-- New York Newsdesk 212 859-1610
